title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from pp.47-48. S is a set with a topology τ. T ⊂ S is a subset, presumably closed, and U = S∖T is its complement; p.47 writes 'T∖S', which is a slip. On T we are given a new topology τ'_0. On p.47 Grothendieck defines τ' on S by its closed sets: X is τ'-closed iff 1° X∩U is closed in U for τ|U; 2° X∩T is τ'_0-closed; 3° (closure of X∩U in τ)∩T ⊂ X∩T. In other words, τ' keeps the topology of the open part U and the 'gluing' map from closed subsets of U to subsets of T (A ↦ closure_τ(A)∩T), and replaces the topology on the closed part by τ'_0. This is a recollement of topologies in the spirit of SGA4 open/closed gluing.

He wants a universal characterization of τ' (property e)). The candidate is: τ' is the unique τ'' with (i) τ''≤τ, (ii) τ''|T=τ'_0, (iii) τ''|U=τ|U, (iv) a compatibility condition. Conditions (i)-(iii) give τ''≤τ'. For the converse, condition 3° requires that for A⊂U the τ''-closure of A is τ-closed.

On p.48 he first asks whether closure_{τ'}(A)∩T is τ-closed, as he would need for (iv) as stated. He suspects this is false (margin: 'C'est peut-être faux?') and confirms it with a small finite counterexample. The figure seems to show finite ordered sets or graphs I', I, J, J' with a map φ between two configurations; the elements are 'figures'. With A={b}, the τ-closure is I' tout entier but the τ'-closure is {a,b}. So (iv) in its p.47 form fails.

He then repairs the characterization. The right condition is the 'obvious' one: for every A⊂U, the closures of A for τ and for τ' coincide; this already implies τ|U=τ'|U. Then the closure of an arbitrary A⊂S is given explicitly by

closure_{τ'}(A) = closure_τ(A∩U) ∪ closure_{τ'_0}(A∩T).

The purpose is to construct and characterize a modified topology on a 'space of figures' in which the stratum T gets a new topology while the open stratum and the gluing are unchanged. This is a technical lemma for chapter V, 'Algèbre des figures'.
errors: p.47 writes U = T∖S; it should be S∖T (p.48 has it right).
Condition (iv) as stated on p.47 is not the right characterizing condition. Grothendieck finds this himself with a counterexample on p.48.

The final closure formula is correct only if closure_τ(A∩U)∩T is τ'_0-closed. That holds when τ'_0 is finer than τ|T, or in general when the gluing condition 3° is respected; this hypothesis is implicit and not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Gluing a topology from a topology on an open part U, a topology on the closed complement T, and the closure (gluing) map from U to T; changing the topology on the closed stratum only
ideas.modern_name: recollement of topologies / stratified spaces (open–closed gluing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Artin–Verdier, SGA4 (recollement of topoi); classical point-set topology
ideas.where_published: SGA4 exposé IV (recollement), in the topos setting

ideas.what: Characterizing the glued topology by its restrictions to U and T plus the invariance of closures of subsets of U
ideas.modern_name: universal characterization of a glued (recollement) topology

ideas.what: Finite counterexample using a small configuration of finite ordered sets / figures

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine point-set lemma about gluing a topology along an open/closed decomposition, with a self-correction by a small counterexample. It is the end of a working session, with no new mathematics beyond standard recollement ideas.
transcription_corrections: Line 'C'est même [?] faux en effet' is a reconstructed reading of an uncertain line, under the margin note 'C'est peut-être faux?'. Probably 'C'est effectivement faux' or similar, followed by 'en voici un contre-exemple' or similar.

Text beside the figure reads roughly: 'I' a trois éléments, I un[?], [?] deux, J un seul, J' deux. On prend A = {b}, son adhérence pour τ est I' tout entier, pour τ' c'est {a,b}.' ('si adhérence' should be 'son adhérence').

'Finalement, la condition (iv) devient' is more likely 'Finalement, la condition (iv) revient à imposer à τ' par les conditions sur τ̄ ... c'est la condition évidente : pour A ⊂ U = S∖T, ses adhérences pour τ et pour τ' sont égales (ce qui implique déjà τ|U = τ'|U)'.
'Cela donne l'adhérence de A pour un quelconque A' should be 'Cela donne l'adhérence d'une partie quelconque A, comme ...'.
Final formula: the union sign is correct: closure_{τ'}(A) = closure_τ(A∩U) ∪ closure_{τ'_0}(A∩T).
